title: Tech Note: 4D Deployment Options for Wide Area Networks
author: Jason T. Slack, Technical Support Engineer, 4D Inc.

historical_commentary.text: This note surveys architectural options for reaching a 4D Client/Server database over a WAN circa 2007 — web-based access (Web 1.0 pages, the emerging 4D Ajax Framework, SOAP/REST web services), server-centric remoting (Terminal Services, Citrix), and remote-desktop tools (VNC, Apple Remote Desktop) — because native 4D Client/Server was only supported and performant on a LAN. The specific mention of the 4D Ajax Framework and 4D Web 2.0 Pack is now obsolete, and 4D's own remote connectivity story has since evolved (e.g., improved client/server networking and cloud-friendly deployment), but the underlying architectural trade-offs it describes (thin web client vs. remoted desktop vs. optimized fat client over WAN) remain a genuinely useful and still-relevant framework for reasoning about deploying a client/server database application across a WAN today.
related_updates: 4D Ajax Framework and 4D Web 2.0 Pack, mentioned as a Web 2.0 option, were later discontinued
4D's client/server networking and remote access options have been improved and expanded in later 4D versions
The general architectural options discussed (web-based, server-centric/remoted desktop) remain standard approaches to WAN deployment of client/server applications today
